key_insight: A physics-informed CNN-LSTM can forecast long-term perovskite photoluminescence degradation from early time-series data, even for unseen materials.
engineering_relevance: This offers a faster, more interpretable way to screen perovskite stability and reduce the time and cost of accelerated ageing tests.
method: Collected 167 metal halide perovskite samples with varied compositions and crystallinities.
Stressed samples with heat and light while recording >86k photoluminescence spectra.
Used physics-based featurization plus a hybrid CNN-LSTM to predict future PL decay and identify stability descriptors.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the model generalizes across material groups and outperforms baseline benchmarks on a dataset of 167 samples and more than 86k spectra.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and coverage of the training dataset, so extrapolation to new chemistries or test conditions should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Physics-informed time-series forecasting of perovskite photoluminescence stability
